title: Paged KV cache lifecycle: allocation, eviction, fragmentation mitigation
creator: Michael Chen
description: Implement a paged KV cache allocator and eviction policy to support large-context models with minimal fragmentation and predictable memory behavior. This ticket covers allocator design, eviction heuristics for mixed prefill/decode loads, compaction strategies to reduce fragmentation, and runtime knobs for reuse across concurrent decodes.
acceptance_criteria: Paged allocator implemented and toggled behind runtime flag --kv-paged=true
End-to-end perf regression < 2% for 2k context p99 latency under typical load compared to baseline
Memory fragmentation (measured by free vs reserved pages) reduced by >= 30% for long-running continuous workloads
Eviction policy supports generational fallback and provides stable decode throughput when capacity pressure occurs
Unit and integration tests covering allocation, eviction, compaction, and reuse behaviors
Documentation in runtime docs explaining knobs, metrics, and recommended configs for Dedicated/Private
technical_notes: Allocator model: fixed-size page allocator (4KB and 64KB page classes) with slab-like region management to avoid small-chunk fragmentation
KV entries mapped to pages; large KV rows (long sequences) span contiguous pages and are pinned during decode unless eviction required
Eviction: hybrid generational LRU where prefill pages are marked lower-priority than decode-active pages; on pressure prefer evicting cold-prefill pages first
Compaction: background compaction thread performs hole consolidation at region boundaries using copy-on-write snapshots to avoid blocking active decodes
Reuse: maintain per-worker hot-page caches to reuse previously-allocated pages for same model/version pairs across requests to reduce allocation churn
Prefill/Decode scheduling: prioritize prefill work during low latency budgets, and perform speculative prefetch of KV pages for upcoming decodes using access-pattern histograms
Metrics: page_allocs, page_frees, page_evictions, fragmentation_ratio, compaction_runs_ms, pinned_page_count, hot_cache_hits
Tradeoffs: more aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but increases transient CPU and copy bandwidth; choose conservative defaults for shared Dedicated hosts
implementation_plan: 1) Add page allocator subsystem: implement page classes, free lists, per-worker caches (ENG-5471-A)
2) Wire KV store to use paged allocator for all new model loads and optional migration path for existing in-memory blobs (ENG-5471-B)
3) Implement eviction policy with generational tags and eviction walker that skips pinned decode pages (ENG-5471-C)
4) Add background compaction worker and snapshot-safe move logic; ensure memory safety with RCU-style pointer swaps (ENG-5471-D)
5) Expose runtime flags and configuration schema in config service (max_pages_per_model, gen_eviction_threshold, compaction_batch_ms) (ENG-5471-E)
6) Add observability: stats, tracing spans for allocations/evictions, and Grafana dashboards (ENG-5471-F)
7) End-to-end perf run, tune defaults for Dedicated SLAs and document recommended settings (ENG-5471-G)
8) QA: add synthetic workloads (prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, mixed) and validate SLOs and memory stability (ENG-5471-H)
tests: Unit tests for allocator free/alloc edge cases and multi-threaded allocation
Integration test: simulate 10k sequential prefill requests and assert fragmentation_ratio < 0.4
Eviction test: force memory pressure and ensure cold-prefill eviction order and no eviction of pinned decode pages
Compaction regression test: verify live traffic set memory remains correct during compaction and decode latency impact < 5% during compaction windows
Fuzz allocation with randomized sizes to detect boundary conditions and leaks
Performance benchmark: p50/p95/p99 for 1k/2k/8k contexts compared to baseline runtime-2.3
rollout_plan: Feature gated rollout: default off in hosted, opt-in in Dedicated/Private via runtime flag
Canary: enable on 5% of hosts using runtime-2.4-canary image, collect metrics for 48h
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 1 week with automated rollback if compaction_runs_ms > threshold or fragmentation_ratio increases
Fallback: automatic fallback to legacy allocator on OOM or if telemetry indicates >1% request failures during canary
Post-rollout: schedule 1-week observation window and host-level memory/latency postmortem
dependencies: ENG-5332 (KV store refactor: pointer stability and snapshot API)
ENG-5399 (Tracing: allocation/eviction spans and metrics plumbing)
DES-304 (Console: add new KV cache metrics to runtime dashboard)
